h168750891744: This is not a feature brochure but a scorecard built by reading through 139,000 lines of source code layer by layer: 17 dimensions, 8 competitors, and every conclusion traceable to a file and a function. The verdict up front—as a local manager alone, it ranks first in this tier (90.8 / 100); cloud and multi-device, collaboration and community, localization, and cross-platform are not abandoned but sequenced later as long-term goals. Under the same 17-dimension scheme, today's progress scores 71.2 (3rd), while scoring against target values reaches 87.1 (1st). All three numbers are correct; they differ only in "which day you count".

hd0000b5a8124: Why it ranks first on local
h55d9ec6483ed: The data model is a "library" rather than an "album": 36 tables, 15 triggers, 30 indexes (foreign keys already handle cascades), an FTS5 trigram full-text index; 11 kinds of design files, 40+ RAW formats, 9 3D formats, and EPUB e-books can all enter the library and produce thumbnails.
h7941bbe0fe7c: Automation is native: 10 capture sources, 11 MCP tools, a plugin sandbox, REST with token and scope, and /api/docs generating 387 endpoints plus examples in curl, JS, and Python—peers generally offer only "import + drag and drop".
hcc7cef257cdb: Desktop integration reaches the system layer: tray, remappable global hotkeys, Windows live wallpaper (WorkerW + GLSL), drag-out to Explorer, right-click capture, and read-only LAN sharing.
hc0146c474b2d: What each of the four long-term goals is worth
h0798b3fde789: Cloud and multi-device 15 → 80 (weight 9): accounts and read-only multi-device first, then incremental sync and mobile; delivers +5.85.
he99d9da23252: Collaboration and community 20 → 60 (weight 8): comments, sharing, and a least-privilege workflow; no commitment to a plugin marketplace; delivers +3.20.
hefd9e1936a66: Localization 5 → 90 (weight 5): extract UI copy into string entries first, then add a translation layer; delivers +4.25.
h284a22701add: Cross-platform 20 → 85 (weight 4): mac hardware smoke test + installer, Linux deferred; delivers +2.60.
h7e0dc177bc15: The four total +15.9: 71.2 → 87.1, from 3rd to 1st. For order and prerequisites, see Section 09.
hcb937541ba2e: If you are one person, one Windows machine, one local library of tens to hundreds of thousands of assets, this is currently the best choice for value and control; the four long-term goals are directions it genuinely intends to pursue, but their order is set by real constraints—a personal project, no server budget, single-platform maintenance cost—so don't expect them to arrive "in the next release".
h7ec9c1da4561:
A good fit today: a designer's personal library / a photography post-processing asset pool / asset collection and archiving / workflows that need to be driven by scripts and AI.
Still missing today: team sharing, cross-device sync, and localized UI for international markets—they are on the roadmap, not in today's installer.
h23d3f4397eca: Three tiers, all on a 100-point scale, and with the same denominator (17 dimensions, 100 points of weight): ① 71.2 = today (the four platform capabilities scored at today's progress, 3rd); ② 76.4 = mid-term target (read-only multi-device + mac hardware + a permissions prototype, 2nd); ③ 87.1 = long-term target (the four scored at their target values of 80 / 60 / 90 / 85, 1st). The three tiers are monotonically increasing: 71.2 → 76.4 → 87.1; the long-term target is never below today. There is also another yardstick: the local-only track at 90.8 (13 dimensions, 100 points, counting only implemented capabilities, used to compare "local managers" against competitors). Its denominator removes the 26 points of platform weight not yet delivered, so 90.8 and 87.1 cannot be subtracted directly—the equivalent under the same scheme is 71.2.
hd6e8a6170c8f: How to read the scores: above 90 = close to the commercial ceiling for the category; 80–90 = mature and shippable, needing only polish; 70–80 = usable but clearly behind the leaders; below 60 = a structural gap that patches cannot fix. The differences between this audit (2026-11-17) and the previous version (2026-11-16) come from two substantive improvements: ① the collage-save will-download async bug is fixed (Electron's synchronous event cannot use an async handler; the earlier dialog and Chromium's default behavior produced two), eliminating a P1-level bug; ② competitor Eagle 4.0 B22 (2026 Q4) shipped an AI Search plugin + Web API v2, raising Eagle's AI dimension from 65 to 72 and slightly improving automation; Immich v3.4.0 (2026-11) widens GPU coverage in ML v2; PhotoPrism added full-model NVIDIA CUDA acceleration in 2026-10. TuKu's own dimension scores hold: the table count is corrected from 40 to 36 (a factual revision; the feature surface is complete), and the local score moves from 90.9 to 90.8.

h7a3adcf85c4a: Local baseline assumes one machine, one library, one user. What decides the daily experience is then "can I find it again quickly"—organization at 10 points plus retrieval at 12 points are the highest weights of all, followed by performance at 9.
h98e0f11ae094: Long-term 17-dimension assumes that one day it will be compared with products like Immich that "can hold an entire team". There, sync and collaboration total 17 points and localization and cross-platform 9 points, diluting the first 13 dimensions to 74—the four dimensions score 71.2 at today's progress and 87.1 at their target values.

h5a2378df8d74:
Only two walls remain: ① buying a certificate to sign the build (this decides "can it be handed to someone else"); ② acceptance testing on real mac / Linux hardware (no testing, no support claim). Everything else is polish and can wait.

This version (1.2.22 / 2026-11-17) fixes a collage save that stacked two "Save As" dialogs: will-download is a synchronous event, and declaring the handler async let Chromium's default behavior pop an empty dialog first, with our own dialog.showSaveDialog popping a second. Making the handler synchronous and starting the follow-up flow in an async IIFE is enough. The root cause is not rapid clicking (downloadDedupe already deduplicates) but the async declaration itself — a single click was enough to trigger both.

The previous version (1.2.21) added a "hot update" channel: patches to server/** and front-end artifacts can ship as a small signed package that the client layers over the installed build, so a full reinstall is no longer needed — the manifest is Ed25519-signed, seq strictly increases to prevent downgrades, and shellVersion and schemaVersion act as two gates.

Fixed in earlier versions (code locations included, traceable if you are interested): automatic fallback to CPU when the GPU backend crashes in the DML driver; module evaluation depending on the read-only asar directory, which made "A JavaScript error" abort startup; grid layout changed from a full O(n) recomputation to incremental append plus bottom-edge bucketing; no more retries after GPU state is recorded in device-state.json; the AI night batch queue moves semantic/face indexing that cannot finish during the day to idle hours.

h917e6ba7666c: The four long-term goals: 71.2 today, 87.1 once delivered
h1081ac82fce3: First, clear up what is easy to misread: these four are not "explicitly rejected", but long-term goals sequenced after single-machine capabilities. This version (1.2.29 / 2026-11-19) closes the capture inbox loop: capture / upload / paste / phone upload can land in the inbox first, be cleared in bulk from the sidebar, and be switched off in Settings. The previous version (1.2.22 / 2026-11-17) fixed the collage save bug that stacked two "Save as" dialogs: will-download is a sync event, and an async handler lets Chromium's default behavior show a blank dialog before our own dialog.showSaveDialog opens a second one. A sync handler plus an async IIFE for the follow-up work fixes it.The root cause was not double-clicking (downloadDedupe already handled that) but the async declaration itself — one click was enough to trigger both.

The version before that (1.2.21) added the hotfix channel: patches to server/** and the web bundle can ship as a small signed package layered over the installer, with no full reinstall — Ed25519-signed manifests, a strictly increasing seq to block downgrades, and shellVersion + schemaVersion gates.
